title: Billakanti and Shin, "At-Risk Transformation for U.S. Recession Prediction" (International Journal of Forecasting, conditionally accepted): first Linux run, main paper
paper: Rahul Billakanti and Minchul Shin, At-Risk Transformation for U.S. Recession Prediction, International Journal of Forecasting, conditionally accepted
cost_basis: GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04 runner, free for public repositories (a comparable 4 vCPU cloud machine is about 0.20 USD an hour)

environment_commands.cmd: uv --version; pdftoppm -v 2>&1 | head -1; nproc; free -g | head -2; program_v04/.venv/bin/python -c 'import sys,numpy,sklearn,xgboost;print(sys.version);print(numpy.__version__,sklearn.__version__,xgboost.__version__)' || true

setup.cmd: python -m pip install --quiet uv && sudo apt-get install -y -q poppler-utils >/dev/null && uv --version
cd program_v04 && uv sync --locked && cd .. && uv pip install --python program_v04/.venv/bin/python xlrd==2.0.2

scope_notes: Main paper only: Tables 1-7 as CSV. LaTeX tables carry a run fingerprint comment and figures are PDFs, so they are not compared here. The appendix (Tables 8-22, Figure 4) is not run.
The tested platform is macOS on Apple Silicon. This is an x86-64 Linux runner, so the run also says whether the results carry across platforms.
deviations: Run 2 runs only the README's main-paper command (Figures 1-3, Tables 1-7), because the full run passed this runner's time limit in run 1.

The package's own comparison script checks all 50 outputs and so cannot run on the main paper alone. Instead the seven regenerated main-table CSVs are copied over the committed reference CSVs, and receiptgen compares each with the committed file, number by number, at relative tolerance 1e-12. The package's own rule is absolute 5e-12; both are given in the notes.
